rationale: Evidence from race 2 (best so far, score 644.8): the oval finishes 20/20 in 1.92 s with rms 0.009. The s-bend finishes 18/20 (2 off-track exits, progress 0.98). The slalom fails 20/20, with progress 0.26, max_error at the 0.06 m off-track limit, and one line-loss event per run. Steering oscillation on the slalom is low (0.20), so the failure looks like under-correction on sharp direction changes rather than jitter. The wider sensor spread and kd 1.4 both helped: slalom progress rose from 0.16 to 0.26 and the s-bend score rose. Changes: (1) kp 3.0 -> 3.5 for more steering authority on sharp direction changes; kd 1.4 -> 1.6 to keep the damping ratio roughly constant as kp rises. (2) sensor_size 0.012 -> 0.016 m. Larger footprints keep at least one sensor on the 25 mm tape when the robot is off-centre, which should reduce line-loss events, the main slalom failure mode. (3) base_speed stays at 1.2, since the oval has time headroom and the slalom appears limited by steering rather than speed. Geometry (sensor spread +/-0.05 at y 0.07, mass 0.6, track 0.12, radius 0.03) is unchanged, so the effects of the controller and sensor-size changes can be read directly. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.4 with fewer line losses, and s-bend completion at or near 20/20 without losing the oval finish. Hypotheses: (a) slalom exits are caused by line loss at sharp reversals, so larger sensors should reduce line_loss_events; (b) kp 3.5 gives enough authority without the oscillation seen at kp 4 in race 0. Measurements to check next: per-track progress and completion, line_loss_events per track, max_error location, steering_oscillation, and completion_time to see whether speed is becoming a limit.
